work: Enarratio in Epistolam B. Pauli ad Philemonem
source: Dionysii Cartusiani Opera Omnia, t. XIII (Montreuil)

1.title: [Titulus in transcriptione deest]
1.title_en: Exposition of the Epistle to Philemon
1.note: The printed title of this article was not transcribed.

paras.t: Paulus vinctus Jesu Christi, id est pro Christo Romæ ligatus ac incarceratus. Non adjecit, Apostolus, quod est nomen dignitatis, quoniam deprecatoriam scribit epistolam, in qua humilitas convenientius suffragatur ad impetrandum quod petitur. Et Timotheus frater : quem sibi adjungit Apostolus, quoniam dilectus fuerat Philemoni. Idcirco ejus nomine audito, amplius movebatur ad exauditionem. Scribunt vel mandant Philemoni dilecto et adjutori nostro in opere Dei, et Appiæ, conjugi ejus, sorori nostræ spirituali carissimæ, et Archippo commilitoni nostro, id est nobiscum pro Christo militanti atque pugnanti contra adversarios veritatis. Hic Archippus fuit filius Philemonis, Colossensiumque episcopus, de quo ad Colossenses dicitur : Archippo dicite : Vide ministerium tuum, etc. Et ecclesiæ, id est congregationi fidelium, quæ in domo tua est. Omnes hos nominat, ut orent Philemonem pro causa hac, videlicet ut ignoscat Onesimo.
paras.en: [[1:1|Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus|Paulus vinctus Jesu Christi]], that is, bound and imprisoned at Rome for Christ. He did not add *Apostle*, which is a title of dignity, because he is writing a letter of entreaty, in which humility is the more fitting help toward obtaining what is asked. [[1:1|and Timothy, a brother|Et Timotheus frater]]: whom the Apostle joins to himself because he had been dear to Philemon; so that, on hearing his name, Philemon would be the more moved to grant the request. They write, or send word, [[1:1|to Philemon, our beloved and fellow labourer|Philemoni dilecto et adjutori nostro]] in the work of God, [[1:2|And to Appia|et Appiæ]], his wife, [[1:2|our dearest sister|sorori nostræ spirituali carissimæ]] in the spirit, [[1:2|and to Archippus, our fellow soldier|et Archippo commilitoni nostro]], that is, one who soldiers with us for Christ and fights against the adversaries of the truth. This Archippus was the son of Philemon and bishop of the Colossians, of whom it is said in the letter to the Colossians: [[Col 4:17|say to Archippus: Take heed to the ministry|Archippo dicite : Vide ministerium]] [Denis reads *Vide ministerium tuum*, 'Take heed to thy ministry'], etc. [[1:2|and to the church|Et ecclesiæ]], that is, to the congregation of the faithful, [[1:2|which is in thy house|quæ in domo tua est]]. He names all these so that they may entreat Philemon in this cause, namely that he forgive Onesimus.

paras.t: Gratia vobis et pax detur, augeatur et conservetur a Deo Patre nostro, id est Patre æterno, et Domino Jesu Christo, Filio, quem omnia effecit Pater.
paras.en: [[1:3|Grace to you and peace|Gratia vobis et pax]] be given, increased and preserved [[1:3|from God our Father|a Deo Patre nostro]], that is, the eternal Father, [[1:3|and from the Lord Jesus Christ|et Domino Jesu Christo]], the Son, through whom the Father made all things[[John 1:3||]].

paras.t: Gratias ago Deo meo semper, id est omni tempore opportuno, memoriam tui, o Philemon, faciens, id est tui reminiscens, in orationibus meis, quas fundo pro te ceterisque fidelibus, audiens a narrantibus caritatem tuam et fidem quam habes in Domino Jesu, id est ad gloriam ejus, vel virtute ipsius, vel in ipso sicut in objecto, amando et credendo in eum, et in omnes sanctos, id est, per opera bona extendis ac manifestas caritatem tuam et fidem in omnes Christianos tecum exsistentes seu tibi occurrentes, quos diligis, foves, eisque credis et fideliter subvenis; ut communicatio fidei tuæ, id est operatio tua fidelis, sive largitio qua bona tua ex fide communicas aliis, evidens fiat, id est, Deo per approbationem innotescat, in agnitione omnis boni, id est in notitia mentis divinæ, cui omnia bona clarissime illucescunt : evidens, inquam, fiat in Christo Jesu, id est per Christum, cujus auxilio ad hoc pervenitur. Vel, In agnitione omnis boni, id est in attestatione omnium operum bonorum, qua Christus in die judicii attestabitur operibus justorum, dicendo : Nudus fui et cooperuistis me, etc. Ad hoc itaque bene agis, ut Christus in die judicii opera tua approbet et declaret justa fuisse.
paras.en: [[1:4|I give thanks to my God|Gratias ago Deo meo]] [[1:4|always|semper]], that is, at every fitting time, [[1:4|making a remembrance of thee|memoriam tui]], O Philemon, that is, calling thee to mind, [[1:4|in my prayers|in orationibus meis]], which I pour out for thee and the rest of the faithful, [[1:5|Hearing|audiens]] from those who tell of it [[1:5|of thy charity and faith, which thou hast in the Lord Jesus|caritatem tuam et fidem quam habes in Domino Jesu]], that is, unto his glory, or by his power, or in him as in their object, by loving him and believing in him, [[1:5|and towards all the saints|et in omnes sanctos]], that is, by good works thou extendest and showest thy charity and faith toward all the Christians who live with thee or come thy way, whom thou lovest and cherishest, and whom thou trustest and faithfully helpest [Denis plays on *fides*: faith in God, and trust and good faith toward men]; [[1:6|That the communication of thy faith|ut communicatio fidei tuæ]], that is, thy faithful working, or the largess by which, out of faith, thou sharest thy goods with others, [[1:6|may be made evident|evidens fiat]], that is, may become known to God by his approving it, [[1:6|in the acknowledgment of every good|in agnitione omnis boni]], that is, in the knowledge of the divine mind, to which all good things shine forth most clearly: may be made evident, I say, [[1:6|in Christ Jesus|in Christo Jesu]], that is, through Christ, by whose help this is attained. Or, [[1:6|in the acknowledgment of every good|In agnitione omnis boni]], that is, in the attestation of all good works, by which Christ on the day of judgment will bear witness to the works of the just, saying: [[Matt 25:36|Naked, and you covered me|Nudus fui et cooperuistis me]], etc. So thou doest well to this end, that Christ on the day of judgment may approve thy works and declare them to have been just.

paras.t: Gaudium enim spirituale magnum habui et consolationem in adversis meis, in caritate tua, id est ex consideratione operum tuæ dilectionis. Sic quippe patrem suum filius sapiens lætificat. Quia viscera sanctorum, id est interiores affectus, et etiam interiora corporis fidelium, dolore vel fame, aut simili passione afflicti, requieverunt per te, frater, id est, a te refocillata consolataque sunt, dum fideles pie recepisti ac sustentasti.
paras.en: [[1:7|For I have had great joy|Gaudium enim spirituale magnum habui]], a spiritual joy, [[1:7|and consolation|et consolationem]] in my adversities, [[1:7|in thy charity|in caritate tua]], that is, from considering the works of thy love. For it is thus that [[Prov 10:1|A wise son maketh the father glad|patrem suum filius sapiens lætificat]]. [[1:7|because the bowels of the saints|Quia viscera sanctorum]], that is, the inward affections [*viscera*, 'bowels', the inward parts, taken for the heart and its affections], and also the inward parts of the bodies of the faithful, afflicted with pain or hunger or some like suffering, [[1:7|have been refreshed by thee, brother|requieverunt per te, frater]], that is, have been revived and comforted by thee, when thou didst kindly receive and support the faithful.

paras.t: Propter quod, videlicet quia tam caritative te habes, ego multam fiduciam habens in Christo Jesu, id est per gratiam Christi, vel secundum voluntatem ipsius, imperandi tibi, quum sim apostolus, quod ad rem pertinet, id est, quod tuam salutem concernit et petitione condignum est ; propter caritatem nostram ad invicem magis obsecro quod imperare valebam, quum sis talis ut Paulus, senex, id est, quum mihi sis similis vita et senio, nunc autem Paulus est et vinctus Jesu Christi, id est pro Christo.
paras.en: [[1:8|Wherefore|Propter quod]], namely because thou bearest thyself so charitably, I, [[1:8|though I have much confidence in Christ Jesus|multam fiduciam habens in Christo Jesu]], that is, through the grace of Christ, or according to his will, [[1:8|to command thee|imperandi tibi]], since I am an apostle, [[1:8|that which is to the purpose|quod ad rem pertinet]], that is, what concerns thy salvation and is well worth the asking; [[1:9|For charity sake|propter caritatem]], our charity toward one another, [[1:9|I rather beseech|magis obsecro]] what I could have commanded, [[1:9|whereas thou art such a one, as Paul, an old man|quum sis talis ut Paulus, senex]], that is, since thou art like me in life and in age; [[1:9|and now|nunc autem]] Paul is [[1:9|a prisoner also of Jesus Christ|et vinctus Jesu Christi]], that is, for Christ.

paras.t: Consequenter forma petitionis inducitur. Obsecro te pro meo filio spirituali, quem genui quantum ad esse spirituale, perducendo eum ad fidem et gratiam, ego exsistens in vinculis Romæ, ubi et eum baptizavi : filio, inquam, Onesimo, qui tibi aliquando inutilis fuit, quando bona tua subtraxit, nunc autem conversus a me, tibi et mihi utilis est. Pro te enim orat, et mihi ministrat. Quem remisi tibi, ut tibi reconcilietur et satisfaciat. Tu autem illum ut mea viscera, id est filium meum mihi intime cordialiterque dilectum, suscipe pie et caritative.
paras.en: Next the form of the request is set out. [[1:10|I beseech thee for my son|Obsecro te pro meo filio]], my spiritual son, [[1:10|whom I have begotten|quem genui]] as to his spiritual being, by bringing him to faith and grace, while I was [[1:10|in my bands|in vinculis]] at Rome, where I also baptized him: my son, I say, [[1:10|Onesimus|Onesimo]], [[1:11|Who hath been heretofore unprofitable to thee|qui tibi aliquando inutilis fuit]], when he made off with thy goods, [[1:11|but now|nunc autem]], converted by me, [[1:11|is profitable both to me and thee|tibi et mihi utilis]]. For he prays for thee, and serves me. [[1:12|Whom I have sent back to thee|Quem remisi tibi]], that he may be reconciled to thee and make amends. [[1:12|And do thou receive him as my own bowels|Tu autem illum ut mea viscera]], that is, as my son, loved by me inwardly and from the heart: [[1:12|receive|suscipe]] him kindly and charitably.

paras.t: Quem ego volueram quadam vice mecum detinere, ut pro te, id est loco et vice tuæ personæ, mihi ministraret in vinculis Evangelii, id est mihi vincto propter Evangelii prædicationem. Sine tuo autem consilio prævio nihil volui facere in hoc negotio voluntate perfecta, quamvis ante volueram eum detinere, uti non velut ex necessitate bonum tuum esset, id est, ut servitus quam Onesimus mihi pro te impenderet, non esset tibi displicens atque molesta, sed voluntarium, id est, ex tuo consensu procederet, sicque tibi meritoria fieret. Debes ergo eum recipere.
paras.en: [[1:13|Whom I would have|Quem ego volueram]] at one time [[1:13|retained with me|mecum detinere]], [[1:13|that in thy stead|ut pro te]], that is, in the place and stead of thy person, [[1:13|he might have ministered to me in the bands of the gospel|mihi ministraret in vinculis Evangelii]], that is, to me, bound for preaching the gospel. [[1:14|But without thy counsel|Sine tuo autem consilio]] given beforehand [[1:14|I would do nothing|nihil volui facere]] in this business with a full will [that is, with a settled and complete will, as against the mere wish he had before], although earlier I had wished to keep him, [[1:14|that thy good deed might not be as it were of necessity|uti non velut ex necessitate bonum tuum esset]], that is, that the service which Onesimus would render me in thy stead might not be displeasing and irksome to thee, [[1:14|but voluntary|sed voluntarium]], that is, that it might proceed from thy consent, and so become meritorious for thee. Thou oughtest therefore to receive him.

paras.t: Forsitan enim ideo, saltem per occasionem et indirecte, discessit ad horam, id est per tempus aliquantulum, a te, ut æternum, id est sine fine tibi sociandum, scilicet in præsenti et in futuro, illum reciperes. Hac fuit una causa fugæ ejus indirecta, id est non intenta ab Onesimo; sed Deus propter eam permisit eum discedere, sicut permisit Joseph vendi propter salutem multorum.
paras.en: [[1:15|For perhaps he therefore|Forsitan enim ideo]], at least by way of occasion and indirectly, [[1:15|departed for a season|discessit ad horam]], that is, for a little while, [[1:15|from thee|a te]], so that [[1:15|for ever|ut æternum]], that is, as one to be joined to thee without end, namely in the present life and in the life to come, [[1:15|thou mightest receive him again|illum reciperes]]. This was one indirect cause of his flight, that is, one not intended by Onesimus; but God permitted him to depart for its sake, as he permitted Joseph to be sold[[Gen 45:5||]] for the salvation of many[[Gen 50:20||]].

paras.t: Jam non ut servum ut ante, sed pro servo, qualis fuit, carissimum fratrem in fide et caritate, maxime mihi qui eum converti ; quanto autem magis tibi carissimus esse debet, et in carne, id est quia servus tuus, et in Domino, id est propter gratiam Dei exsistentem in eo ! Quanto enim tibi vicinior, tanto et carior esse debet.
paras.en: [[1:16|Not now as a servant|Jam non ut servum]], as before, [[1:16|but instead of a servant|sed pro servo]], such as he was, [[1:16|a most dear brother|carissimum fratrem]] in faith and charity, [[1:16|especially to me|maxime mihi]], who converted him; [[1:16|But how much more to thee|quanto autem magis tibi]] ought he to be most dear, [[1:16|both in the flesh|et in carne]], that is, because he is thy servant, [[1:16|and in the Lord|et in Domino]], that is, because of the grace of God dwelling in him! For the nearer he is to thee, the dearer too he ought to be.

paras.t: Si ergo habes me socium, id est, si ita me diligis ut socium, suscipe illum affectuose et reverenter, sicut me susciperes, si venirem ad te. Si autem, id est quia, aliquid nocuit tibi, aut debet ad restitutionem ablati, hoc mihi imputa, id est, rationem et satisfactionem exige a me. Ego pro illo me offero. Per hoc omnem excusationem Philemoni aufert Apostolus.
paras.en: [[1:17|If therefore thou count me a partner|Si ergo habes me socium]], that is, if thou lovest me as a partner, [[1:17|receive him|suscipe illum]] with affection and reverence, [[1:17|as myself|sicut me]], as thou wouldst receive me if I came to thee. [[1:18|And if|Si autem]], that is, since, [[1:18|he hath wronged thee in any thing or is in thy debt|aliquid nocuit tibi, aut debet]] for the restoring of what he took, [[1:18|put that to my account|hoc mihi imputa]], that is, demand the reckoning and the satisfaction of me. I offer myself in his place. By this the Apostle takes away from Philemon every excuse.

paras.t: Et ut certus sit Philemon de auctore præsentis epistolæ, subditur : Ego Paulus scripsi mea manu epistolam. Ego reddam pro Onesimo debitum, vel spiritualem compensationem, maxime si exegeris. Quod ideo dico, ut non dicam tibi, quod tamen veraciter dicere possem, videlicet quod et te ipsum mihi debes ad serviendum et obediendum, eo quod sis a me conversus ad fidem : et ideo non indigeo te tantum obsecrare pro causa hac, quia minus peto quam debes.
paras.en: And that Philemon may be sure who wrote this letter, there follows: [[1:19|I Paul have written it with my own hand|Ego Paulus scripsi mea manu]], the letter. [[1:19|I will repay it|Ego reddam]]: the debt for Onesimus, or a spiritual recompense, above all if thou demand it. And this I say so as [[1:19|not to say to thee|ut non dicam tibi]] what I could nevertheless truly say, namely [[1:19|that thou owest me thy own self also|quod et te ipsum mihi debes]], to serve and obey me, since thou wast converted by me to the faith: and so I have no need to entreat thee so much in this cause, since I ask less than thou owest.

paras.t: Ita, frater, id est, sic est ut dico; vel, sic age ut postulo. Quod si feceris, ego te fruar, id est utar, in Domino, id est, de tuo merito seu opere bono gaudebo, et tibi congratulabor spiritualiter in Domino, in præsenti atque futuro. Quod ut impleatur, refice, id est, consolare et fove, viscera mea, id est filium meum Onesimum, vel, cordis mei affectum, in Christo.
paras.en: [[1:20|Yea, brother|Ita, frater]], that is, it is as I say; or, do as I ask. And if thou dost so, I shall [[1:20|enjoy thee|ego te fruar]], that is, have the use of thee [Denis glosses *fruar*, 'enjoy', by *utar*, 'use': in Augustine's distinction God alone is enjoyed for his own sake, and creatures are used for his], [[1:20|in the Lord|in Domino]], that is, I shall rejoice over thy merit or good work, and congratulate thee spiritually in the Lord, in the present and in the future. That this may be fulfilled, [[1:20|Refresh|refice]], that is, console and cherish, [[1:20|my bowels|viscera mea]], that is, my son Onesimus, or the affection of my heart, in Christ [the Vulgate has *in Domino*, 'in the Lord'].

paras.t: Confidens de obedientia tua, scripsi tibi, sciens, id est confidenter præsumens et probabiliter æstimans, quoniam et super id quod dico, id est plus quam deprecor, facies. Hac blanda commendatione, quæ tamen veritati innititur, provocat eum ad meliora. Fit enim frequenter, ut qui videt bene sentiri de se, meliorem se præbeat.
paras.en: [[1:21|Trusting in thy obedience, I have written to thee|Confidens de obedientia tua, scripsi tibi]], [[1:21|knowing|sciens]], that is, confidently presuming and reckoning it likely, that [[1:21|more than I say|quoniam et super id quod dico]], that is, more than I beg, [[1:21|thou wilt also do|facies]]. By this gentle commendation, which yet rests upon the truth, he spurs him on to better things. For it often happens that one who sees that he is well thought of shows himself the better for it.

paras.t: Simul autem et para mihi hospitium, id est, te ipsum para ad recipiendum me, ut inveniam te qualem desidero. (Quid enim necessarium fuit parare hospitium pauperi homini qui pane et aqua contentus erat?) Nam spero per orationes vestras, id est merito precum vestrarum, quas pro mei liberatione Domino jugiter funditis, donari me vobis a Deo, ita quod liberatus de carcere, revertar ad vos.
paras.en: [[1:22|But withal prepare me also a lodging|Simul autem et para mihi hospitium]], that is, prepare thyself to receive me, so that I may find thee such as I desire. (For what need was there to prepare a lodging for a poor man who was content with bread and water[[1 Tim 6:8||]]?) [[1:22|For I hope that through your prayers|Nam spero per orationes vestras]], that is, by the merit of your prayers, which you pour out to the Lord without ceasing for my release, [[1:22|I shall be given unto you|donari me vobis]] by God, so that, freed from prison, I may return to you.

paras.t: Salutat te, id est, salutem tibi dicit et optat, Epaphras (qui erat Colossensis, sicut et Philemon), concaptivus meus in Christo Jesu, id est pro Christo, Marcus evangelista, vel consobrinus Barnabæ, Aristarchus, Demas. In epistola ad Timotheum dixit Apostolus Demam reversum ad sæculum. Si ergo ista epistola scripta fuit post illam, probatur Demas pœnituisse atque redisse ad Paulum, si tamen de eodem sit sermo. Et Lucas evangelista, mihi inseparabiliter fidelissimeque adhærens: qui licet ultimo nominetur, minor tamen non fuit. Adjutores mei.
paras.en: [[1:23|There salute thee|Salutat te]], that is, bids thee health and wishes it thee [*salutem dicere*, to greet, is literally to say 'health'], [[1:23|Epaphras|Epaphras]] (who was a Colossian, as was Philemon also), [[1:23|my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus|concaptivus meus in Christo Jesu]], that is, for Christ; [[1:24|Mark|Marcus]] the evangelist, or the cousin of Barnabas; [[1:24|Aristarchus, Demas|Aristarchus, Demas]]. In the letter to Timothy the Apostle said that Demas had gone back to the world[[2 Tim 4:9||]]. If, then, this letter was written after that one, it is proved that Demas repented and returned to Paul, provided the same man is meant. [[1:24|and Luke|Et Lucas]] the evangelist, who clung to me inseparably and most faithfully: who, though he is named last, was not the least. [[1:24|my fellow labourers|Adjutores mei]].

paras.t: Gratia Domini nostri Jesu Christi sit cum spiritu vestro. Amen. In principio et in fine epistolæ loquitur Apostolus pluribus, in processu vero Philemoni dumtaxat, quia ad eum principaliter sermo dirigitur.
paras.en: [[1:25|The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.|Gratia Domini nostri Jesu Christi sit cum spiritu vestro. Amen]] At the beginning and at the end of the letter the Apostle speaks to several, but in the course of it to Philemon alone, because the discourse is directed chiefly to him.
